channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Crise de Flávio afetou números de Tarcísio em São Paulo? Diretor do Paraná Pesquisas responde
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas maintains his lead in the 2026 São Paulo election polls, with 47.3% in the first round and 52.7% in the second round against Fernando Haddad, despite recent crises involving allies like Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and administrative issues. According to Murilo Hidalgo of Paraná Pesquisas, São Paulo voters distinguish the governor’s personal image from problems involving his allies, which has preserved his polling stability. Haddad struggles to grow due to high electoral rejection, also tied to the negative perception of the Lula government in the state.

item.title: Rachado pela candidatura de Joaquim Barbosa, DC vai expulsar Aldo Rebelo
item.description: The Christian Democracy (DC) party announced the opening of a disciplinary process to expel former minister Aldo Rebelo, following his presidential candidacy being challenged by the affiliation of former Supreme Court minister Joaquim Barbosa, who also plans to run for president in 2026. The decision, made by the party’s national executive, deepens an internal split, with Rebelo stating he may seek legal action to maintain his candidacy. Former deputy Paulo Cesar Quartiero, DC leader in Roraima, withdrew his pre-candidacy for state governor and labeled Barbosa a 'swindler'.

item.title: Ala no Planalto defende indicação de ministra do STJ após rejeição de Messias para vaga no STF
item.description: The Lula administration's inner circle at the Planalto Palace is advocating for the nomination of Minister Daniela Teixeira from the Superior Tribunal of Justice (STJ) to the Supreme Federal Court (STF) following the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias. The pragmatic assessment is that Teixeira was approved with 68 votes in the STJ — double Messias's 34 — offering a technically vetted profile with strong Senate acceptance, fulfilling the goal of appointing a woman to the STF without political risk. Nevertheless, a PT faction continues to push for Messias's re-nomination, despite Senator Alcolumbre stating he will not reconsider the name this year and a 2010 resolution making a new vote in 2026 unfeasible.

item.title: Lula repete “coração coreano” em evento cultural no Espírito Santo
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva repeated the 'Korean heart' hand gesture during the 6th National Teia of Culture Points in Aracruz, Espírito Santo, on May 21, 2026. The gesture, made with thumb and index finger crossed, had previously been used by Lula during his official visit to South Korea in February. The event marked the restart of the initiative after 12 years, with Lula signing a decree to restructure the National Council of Cultural Policy, announcing 89 mobile Ceus units, and delivering identification plaques to over 800 cultural points.

item.title: Congresso derruba vetos de Lula à LDO e flexibiliza repasses a municípios em ano eleitoral
item.description: The National Congress overturned presidential vetoes by Lula on the 2026 Budget Guidelines Law (LDO), easing rules for federal transfers to municipalities during an election year. The measure allows transfers in the three months preceding elections, except for ongoing works or emergencies, and exempts municipalities with up to 65,000 inhabitants from compliance requirements to receive voluntary funds. The move was driven by municipal leaders during the March of Mayors, who argue local investments depend on such resources.

item.title: Lula cita Ricardo Magro pela 1ª vez: “maior devedor do país”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva mentioned businessman Ricardo Magro by name for the first time, referencing him as the country's 'biggest debtor of public money' during a speech at the 6th National Culture Points Network opening in Aracruz (ES). Lula claimed Magro lives in the United States and called for his extradition, stating he had discussed the matter with Donald Trump. He also tied Magro to fuel fraud investigations and criticized Bolsonaro's administration for dismantling cultural policies and allegedly maintaining a 'hate cabinet'.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que quer Vorcaro em CPMI para falar sobre relação com ele, Lula e Moraes
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, requested the National Congress president to read the requirement for installing a CPMI to investigate irregularities at Banco Master, aiming to summon banker Daniel Vorcaro and his former partner Augusto Lima to testify about their ties with him, Lula, and Alexandre de Moraes. He claims he has nothing to hide and accuses left-wing parliamentarians of fearing the investigation, likening the Master scandal to the mensalão and Operation Car Wash, despite not having signed other CPMI requests from deputies of Rede and PSOL and Senator Rogério Carvalho (PT).

item.title: Congresso derruba veto de Lula e permite doações durante campanha eleitoral
item.description: Congress overturned President Lula's veto that prohibited public donations of goods, funds, and benefits during the electoral period, allowing the government to continue such transfers even in the three months preceding elections, provided beneficiaries fulfill obligations. The provision was included in the Budget Guidelines Law (LDO), vetoed by the Executive on grounds of unconstitutionality, but approved by lawmakers who argue it sustains support for municipalities affected by the previous administration.

item.title: Democracia Cristã abre processo para expulsar Aldo Rebelo
item.description: The Christian Democracy party (DC) has initiated a summary expulsion process against Aldo Rebelo, former president of the Chamber of Deputees, following his recent affiliation. The party cites the 'exhaustion' of attempts at harmonious resolution due to Rebelo's dissatisfaction with the DC's decision to launch the pre-candidacy of a former Supreme Court minister.

item.title: Minirreforma eleitoral limita e parcela multa a partidos políticos
item.description: The electoral mini-reform approved by the Chamber of Deputies limits fines for parties with rejected accounts to R$30,000, prohibits blocking of the Party and Electoral Funds, and authorizes mass messaging to registered voters. The symbolic vote without individual registration was criticized by groups like MCCE as a setback for oversight and transparency, while the rapporteur argues the changes are necessary for legal security and party management.

item.title: Democracia Cristã expulsa Aldo Rebelo em meio a racha por candidatura a presidente
item.description: The Christian Democracy party expelled former minister Aldo Rebelo after he was sidelined in favor of Joaquim Barbosa as the party’s presidential pre-candidate, triggering a internal split. The expulsion followed Rebelo’s public criticisms of party leadership, which the party labeled as attacks on its values and statutes.

item.title: Alcolumbre barra CPMI do Master e diz que decisão é dele
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre refused to read the requests to install the CPMI investigating Banco Master, stating the decision rests with the Senate's Directive Board, despite at least five valid requests. He faced pressure from parties including PT and PL, with Flávio Bolsonaro challenging Banco Master founder Daniel Vorcaro to testify and accusing the left of fearing the investigation. Under congressional rules, a CPMI must be read by the Senate president once it reaches 171 signatures to proceed with installation.

item.title: O encontro de Flávio e Eduardo Bolsonaro com Trump: mico ou 'solução'?
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s circle reportedly sees Donald Trump as a potential 'solution' to the legal and political troubles surrounding the senator, suggesting an international alliance as a way out. The exclusive article claims Trump is viewed as a strategic ally to counter domestic pressures. The meeting between Flávio, Eduardo Bolsonaro, and Trump is framed as an effort to strengthen foreign backing amid internal challenges in Brazil.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro articula ida aos EUA para visita a Trump, dizem assessores
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) is reportedly arranging an agenda to visit the United States and meet with former President Donald Trump, according to his advisors. The news outlet sought comment from the White House but has not yet received a response regarding the potential trip.

item.title: Lula diz que nada garante que Trump não vá reivindicar Amazônia como ‘dele’
item.description: President Lula warned that Brazil is 'unguarded' and that nothing guarantees Trump will not claim the Amazon as his own, citing Trump's previous claims over Greenland, Canada, and the Panama Canal. He stressed the need for Brazil to arm itself and take responsibility for protecting the country, drawing parallels to historical threats like the Paraguayan War. Lula also said he seeks a 'war of narratives' with Trump, aiming to prove with data that Brazil is right in its stance on respect and dialogue.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio debate se biografia de Bolsonaro deve ser lançada antes das eleições
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign is debating whether to delay the September release of a biopic about former President Jair Bolsonaro after revelations that banker Daniel Vorcaro financed the film. The new communications team argues that releasing it a month before the election could revive controversy without expanding Flávio's voter base, suggesting a postponement to year-end to protect Bolsonaro's international image. No contact has yet been made with the film's production team.

item.title: “Nós nunca fomos atrás da Lei Daniel Vorcaro”, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula criticized the financing of Jair Bolsonaro's biopic through the Daniel Vorcaro Law, accusing Flávio Bolsonaro of negotiating $24 million with the businessman arrested by the PF. He also condemned the abolition of the Culture Ministry under Bolsonaro, signed decrees to restructure the CNPC and establish a national policy for traditional cultures, and denounced the Planalto's structure for spreading fake news.

item.title: ‘Quem imaginaria que o que parecia o mais santo dos Bolsonaros pegaria milhões para filme’, diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for requesting millions from businessman Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, to finance a film about former President Jair Bolsonaro, saying he seemed the 'holiest' of the Bolsonaro family. Lula added that 'more things will appear' regarding this relationship and reiterated his opposition to the use of artificial intelligence in electoral campaigns, stating that one cannot vote for lies or abstract things.

item.title: DC decide expulsar Aldo Rebelo do partido; político diz que aposta em Joaquim Barbosa é 'afronta'
item.description: The Christian Democracy (DC) party has initiated disciplinary proceedings to expel Aldo Rebelo after he criticized the party's decision to replace him as its presidential pre-candidate with Joaquim Barbosa. Rebelo stated he will maintain his pre-candidacy and called Barbosa's selection an 'affront' to his political principles. The party said Rebelo's actions are incompatible with its values and statutes, and that his expulsion will be reported to the Electoral Justice.

item.title: Lula ironiza Flávio Bolsonaro e críticas à Lei Rouanet: 'Nunca fomos atrás da lei Daniel Vorcaro'
item.description: President Lula (PT) stated that his government never pursued the 'Daniel Vorcaro law' to fund artists, responding to criticism over conversations between former Master banker and presidential pré-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) regarding alleged tax incentives. He mocked the reference to the law as a distraction from his administration’s real priorities. The remarks were made in an interview on Thursday, May 21, 2026.

item.title: Lula cita conversa de Flávio com Vorcaro e diz que 'ainda vai aparecer muito mais coisa'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that more information will emerge regarding the involvement of former banker Daniel Vorcaro in financing the film 'Dark Horse', about Jair Bolsonaro, and referenced Senator Flávio Bolsonaro as having allegedly received millions of dollars for the project. Lula criticized the use of public funds via the Rouanet Law and emphasized that his government did not seek to fund artists using resources tied to Vorcaro, calling for an end to the 'era of lies and violence'.

item.title: Mário Frias responde a Dino através de post no X e diz que retornará ao Brasil no dia 25 para 'esclarecimentos'
item.description: Federal deputy Mário Frias (PL-SP) announced he will return to Brazil on May 25 to respond to a request for information from Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino regarding R$ 2.6 million in Pix amendments sent in 2024 to an NGO linked to the producer of a film about Jair Bolsonaro. Frias stated he is on an official mission in Bahrain, invited by the Bahraini embassy and with the knowledge of Chamber President Hugo Motta, and will make himself available for clarification upon his return. Dino’s request is part of a preliminary investigation into potential irregularities in the fund transfers.

item.title: Davi Alcolumbre se recusa a ler pedido de criação de CPI do Master pedida por Flávio e parlamentares do PT
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre refused to read requests for the establishment of a CPMI on Banco Master during a joint congressional session, stating the agenda was solely to analyze presidential vetoes on the 2026 LDO. Lawmakers, including Flávio Bolsonaro and PT members, pushed for the commission to investigate Daniel Vorcaro and Augusto Lima, linked to Banco Master and the financing of the 'Dark Horse' film about Bolsonaro's 2018 campaign. Alcolumbre invoked Senate internal rules, asserting that reading CPI requests is at the president's discretion, and rejected all petitions to maintain focus on the original agenda.

item.title: Alcolumbre decide não ler requerimento de CPMI do Banco Master
item.description: Congress President Davi Alcolumbre refused to read the request to open a CPMI investigation into Banco Master, stating the session was limited to reviewing President Lula’s veto of an LDO provision allowing federally funded municipalities with up to 65,000 inhabitants in default to receive resources. He said reading CPMI requests is exclusively the presidency’s prerogative and apologized for not accommodating over 11 lawmakers’ request.

item.title: Janja diz que red pill na internet não é “nossa realidade”
item.description: First Lady Janja da Silva stated that the red pill movement online does not reflect the reality Brazil seeks to build, speaking at the opening of the 6th National Teia of Culture Points in Aracruz, ES. She urged cultural spaces to serve as entry points for transforming mindsets, particularly among 12- to 13-year-olds who consume the most hate content via mobile phones. On the same day, President Lula signed two decrees tightening rules for digital platforms to combat violence against women, including mandatory removal of non-consensual intimate images within two hours and mechanisms against AI-generated sexual deepfakes.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro responde, em inglês, que não pediu encontro com Trump: ‘No, I didn’t ask anything’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) denied in English that he requested a meeting with Donald Trump, stating he was only invited and that the White House must confirm if it will happen. He added he speaks English so Lula cannot understand him, and said his campaign proceeds 'one day at a time'.

item.title: Alcolumbre abre sessão conjunta Congresso para analisar veto sobre doações em período eleitoral
item.description: Congress President Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP) opened on Thursday morning (21) a joint session of senators and deputies to analyze the presidential veto on campaign donation regulations during electoral periods. The session aims to determine whether Congress will override or uphold President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s veto of a bill allowing corporate donations in election campaigns. The issue is central to political reform and campaign financing ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: As críticas de Janja à TV Globo por causa de Juliano Cazarré
item.description: First Lady Janja indirectly and directly criticized actor Juliano Cazarré for spreading false information on GloboNews claiming women kill more male partners than men kill female partners. She linked such narratives to the 'red pill' ideology, warning that algorithmic hatred translates into real-world violence against women. Her remarks were made during the 100-day ceremony of the Brazil Pact between the Three Powers to Combat Femicide.

item.title: TSE torna inelegível ex-deputado federal do Ceará por gasto ilícito de recurso público
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) annulled the diploma and declared former federal deputy Heitor Freire (União-CE) ineligible for illicit campaign spending in the 2022 elections, citing unverified allocation of R$618,000 and disproportionate R$1 million in legal and accounting services. The court also annulled the votes he received in 2022, preventing their use by his party, following a unanimous decision by the ministers.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro articula visita à Casa Branca para agenda com Trump, dizem interlocutores
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) received an invitation from the White House to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump, following coordination by his campaign team. The meeting, potentially facilitated by Darren Beattie and Marco Rubio, remains unconfirmed and without a set date, as the senator evaluates the optimal timing. The visit aims to generate a positive agenda amid campaign turmoil linked to his association with banker Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Sancionado cadastro nacional de condenados por violência contra a mulher
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed Law 15.409/2026, establishing the National Register of Persons Convicted of Violence Against Women (CNVM), which centralizes data on individuals definitively convicted of crimes such as femicide, rape, and sexual harassment in a federal system shared across public security agencies. The registry will take effect 60 days after publication in the Official Gazette and will include full names, personal documents, photographs, and fingerprints of offenders, while preserving victim confidentiality. The Presidency issued a partial veto, rejecting the provision to retain data for up to three years after sentence completion, arguing it violates constitutional principles of proportionality and due process.

item.title: TSE: Justiça deve punir uso de deepfake mesmo sem potencial de induzir eleitor a erro
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously upheld a R$15,000 fine against Fortaleza mayor Evandro Leitão (PT) for using deepfake technology in his 2024 campaign. The video, which used AI to generate false statements attributed to celebrities like Taylor Swift, Barack Obama, Tom Cruise, and Cristiano Ronaldo, was deemed unlawful regardless of whether it could mislead voters, based on a TSE resolution banning synthetic audio or video content for electoral purposes.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vai aos Estados Unidos em busca de reunião com Trump, diz pré-campanha
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, will travel to the United States for a meeting with former President Donald Trump, according to his pre-campaign, although the White House has not yet confirmed the encounter. The move comes amid a crisis in his presidential bid, following a Federal Police investigation into alleged requests for funding from banker Daniel Vorcaro for the film 'Dark Horse', about his father, Jair Bolsonaro. The visit reflects efforts to bolster international support amid domestic challenges, while Lula seeks to prevent Trump from interfering in Brazil’s elections.

item.title: Trump convida Flávio Bolsonaro para visita na Casa Branca
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump invited Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for a White House visit following his meeting with Lula. The goal is to highlight Flávio's proximity to Trump after Lula's successful U.S. visit. The invitation came after an audio surfaced in which Flávio asked Daniel Vorcaro for funds to finance a film about Jair Bolsonaro's trajectory to the presidency.

item.title: Bancada do Novo quer derrubar decretos de Lula sobre redes sociais
item.description: The New Party's caucus in the Chamber of Deputies filed a legislative decree bill to nullify the effects of President Lula's new social media regulations signed last Wednesday (20). The initiative seeks to overturn rules that increase platform liability for illegal content and disinformation. The party argues the measures violate freedom of expression and the Marco Civil da Internet.

item.title: Projetos aprovados na Câmara que fragilizam proteção e fiscalização ambiental ainda precisam passar pelo Senado
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved two bills weakening environmental protection: one reduces the Jamanxim National Forest and converts part of it into an Environmental Protection Area (APA), allowing broader land regularization and economic use; the other blocks fines and embargoes based solely on satellite imagery, requiring prior notice to the area administrator. Both were approved under urgency procedures in celebration of 'Agro Day' and now proceed to the Senate for approval before potential presidential sanction.

item.title: Em meio à crise com Vorcaro, Flávio vai viajar aos EUA para tentar encontro com Trump
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) plans to travel to the United States next Monday to attempt a meeting with President Donald Trump, amid a crisis involving banker Daniel Vorcaro. The trip, reportedly coordinated by allies with alleged support from Secretary of State Marco Rubio, aims to strengthen his alignment with Trumpism, regain political momentum, and position him as the leading representative of Bolsonarism in the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Flávio Bolsonaro tenta retomar rédeas de pré-campanha, que segue a reboque de Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro seeks to regain control of his pre-campaign following crises linked to Daniel Vorcaro, replacing his communications chief and adopting a more policy-oriented discourse, notably criticizing the reduction of the workweek as 'inopportune and electoral'. The strategy aims to distance himself from Vorcaro’s influence and rebuild trust with allies who accused him of lying about his ties to the financier.

item.title: Petrobras aprova adesão ao subsídio do governo a combustíveis
item.description: Petrobras approved its adherence to the government's fuel subsidy program to mitigate the impact of potential price adjustments amid rising international oil prices. The measure, pending complementary rules from the Ministry of Finance, aims to preserve the company's commercial flexibility and avoid immediate cost pass-through to consumers, despite pressure to raise prices due to Middle East conflict and oil exceeding $100 per barrel.

item.title: Com Bethânia e Seu Jorge, 'Clássicos do Brasil' anuncia edição 2026
item.description: The Clássicos do Brasil festival announces its 2026 edition, featuring performances by Bethânia and Seu Jorge, taking place from November 6 to December 6 in Recife and Rio de Janeiro. The event returns to the country’s main cultural stages after a period of absence. The article is subscriber-only, requiring registration for full access.

item.title: Por que o governo Lula recuou na tarifa zero do transporte público
item.description: The Lula government has decided to retreat from the zero-fare public transport proposal for the first half of 2026 due to the tight electoral calendar, high estimated costs (between 60.3 and 90 billion reais annually), and prioritization of ending the 6×1 work scale. The initiative, internally dubbed the 'SUS of Public Transport', will be postponed and likely incorporated into Lula's re-election campaign platform.

item.title: Família Bolsonaro corre para ligar Deolane a Lula
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro (PL), former councilman and Senate pre-candidate from Santa Catarina, quickly linked the arrest of lawyer and influencer Deolane Bezerra—connected to the PCC—to President Lula (PT), attempting to associate the public figure with the federal government through narratives of organized crime. Deolane was arrested on Thursday, May 21, in an operation targeting money laundering. The Bolsonaro family’s strategy aims to exploit the case to damage Lula’s image on social media.

item.title: 54,9% acham que Tarcísio será reeleito, indica Paraná Pesquisas
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey shows that 54.9% of São Paulo voters believe Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) will be re-elected in October 2026. In contrast, only 28.6% of respondents expect Fernando Haddad (PT) to win. Just 1.2% backed the former mayor, whose name was not specified in the excerpt.

item.title: A disputa entre Tarcísio e Haddad pelo governo de São Paulo, segundo o Paraná Pesquisas
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) leads the race for São Paulo governor with 47.3% in the first round and 52.7% in the second round, according to a Paraná Pesquisas survey released on May 21, 2026. Fernando Haddad (PT) follows with 33.5% in the first round and 37.6% in the second, while other candidates such as Paulo Serra (PSDB) and Kim Kataguiri (Missão) trail below 5%. The margin of error is 2.5 percentage points.

item.title: Efeito Master: queda de Flávio Bolsonaro deixa Lula isolado na liderança
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro experienced a 5.4 percentage point drop in the Atlas/Bloomberg poll due to the 'Master Effect', linked to his financial dealings with Daniel Vorcaro, former owner of Banco Master, who was arrested for billion-dollar financial frauds. This left Lula isolated in the lead with 47% voting intentions, stable since March. The Liberal Party challenged the poll in Electoral Court, claiming the questions were not neutral.

item.title: A irregularidade eleitoral do presidente Lula ‘esquecida’ pelo TSE
item.description: On May 1, 2024, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva committed electoral illegality by explicitly asking voters to support Guilherme Boulos, then a pre-candidate for mayor of São Paulo, during a period when pre-campaign propaganda is prohibited. The Electoral Justice initially fined Lula R$20,000 and Boulos R$15,000 for antecipated electoral propaganda, later reduced on appeal to R$15,000 and R$10,000. Although a special appeal was filed with the TSE and remains unresolved since March 2025, Lula has since repeated similar violations using official government events to solicit votes.

item.title: Agência de ex-marketeiro de Flávio Bolsonaro tem R$ 99 milhões em contratos com governo federal
item.description: The advertising agency Cálix Propaganda, owned by Marcello Lopes — former marketer for Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign — has secured R$ 99.28 million in federal government contracts from April 2022 to May 2026, originally established under Jair Bolsonaro’s administration and continued under Lula. Lopes departed Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign following a dispute with Daniel Vorcaro, while the senator admitted to meeting banker Vorcaro after the arrest of Sérgio Lima. Key contracts, including a potential R$ 55 million/year deal with the Ministry of Integration and Regional Development, were extended via amendments during Lula’s term.

item.title: Congresso analisa nesta quinta vetos sobre doações a estados e municípios durante período eleitoral
item.description: The National Congress is reviewing presidential vetoes to the 2026 Budget Guidelines Law (LDO) on Thursday, focusing on four provisions with direct electoral impact, including allowing public donations during the election period and waiving fiscal compliance requirements for small municipalities. The Executive vetoed these measures on grounds of unconstitutionality, stating the LDO cannot override the Electoral Law or address non-budgetary matters. Overturning the vetoes requires an absolute majority in a joint session of Congress.

item.title: Cenários preocupantes
item.description: The article argues that, regardless of the outcome of the 2026 elections, Brazil's political future could face a new crossroads, especially if a frontrunner falters or a dark horse emerges. Lula, whose re-election becomes more likely as Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy weakens, is unlikely to miss the runoff — but could lose, triggering significant instability.

item.title: 8 em cada 10 aprovam isenção do IR para quem ganha até R$ 5 mil
item.description: A Locomotiva Institute and QuestionPro survey shows 85% of Brazilians approve the income tax exemption for those earning up to R$ 5,000 monthly, a 2026 measure. This is the most recognized IR change, with 77% awareness, especially among AB classes (85%). Other reforms like faster refunds and pre-filled declarations also have strong support (78-83%), and approval of the exemption is bipartisan, with 88% of right-wing and 90% of left-wing voters in favor.
